title: Bounded reachability search
statement: Let $K_0$ be a natural number, let $\mathrm{orc}$ assign a Boolean to each of four query indices and each finite bit string, let $x$ be a finite bit string, and let $B,P$ be natural numbers. Let $\varphi$ be a Boolean, let $S$ be a machine state, and let $M:\mathbb{Z}\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ be a memory function. Suppose $S.U=S.V=S.T=S.T_2=S.Z=S.ch=S.c=0$, $S$ satisfies $\mathrm{SBd}(B,P)$, and $M(S.Bs+v)=\mathrm{false}$ for every natural number $v<S.K$. Then there is a memory function $M'$ such that the machine has a finite run from the initial configuration to the configuration at the second count-comparison label if $\varphi$ is true, and at the first-search cleanup label otherwise; every configuration before the endpoint satisfies the guard $G(x,B,P)$. At the endpoint, $U=S.K$ and $c$ is the number of indices $v<S.K$ reachable from some $u<S.K$ with a true initial query by a finite sequence of true step queries whose successive indices remain below $S.K$; all other registers retain their values from $S$. Moreover, every position marked true by $M$ is marked true by $M'$, no memory cell outside $\{S.Bs+v:v<S.K\}$ changes, and for each $v<S.K$, $M'(S.Bs+v)$ is true exactly when $v$ has that reachability property.
hypotheses_covered: An oracle assigning a Boolean to each of four query indices and bit strings
replaced:
Let $K_0$ be a natural number, let $orc$ assign a Boolean answer to each of four query
indices and bit strings, and let $x$ be a bit string. Let $B,P$ be natural numbers, let
$\varphi$ be a Boolean, let $S$ be a machine state, and let
$M:\mathbb{Z}\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ be a memory function. Assume that the
coordinates $U,V,T,T_2,Z,ch,c$ of $S$ are all zero, that $S$ satisfies
$\mathrm{SBd}(B,P)$, and that $M(S.Bs+v)$ is false for every natural number $v<S.K$.
Then there is a memory function $M'$ such that the machine reaches a configuration
satisfying its guard, at the label for the second count comparison when $\varphi$ is
true and at the label for the first count otherwise. In that configuration the counter
$U$ equals $S.K$, the counter $c$ equals the number of indices $v<S.K$ for which $v$ is
reachable from some $u<S.K$ with a true initial query, using finitely many true step
queries and keeping every resulting index below $S.K$, and the remaining register values
are those of $S$; moreover, every bit marked in $M$ remains marked in $M'$, no memory
cell outside $\{S.Bs+v:v<S.K\}$ changes, and for each $v<S.K$, $M'(S.Bs+v)$ is true
exactly when $v$ has that reachability property.
